comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations strongly support the high-resolution cryo-EM structure (C36, C37, C49, C50) as a major achievement. All reviewers acknowledge this passes an important threshold for model building accuracy and represents the first near-atomic resolution structure of a fused TRAP transporter.

Significant disagreement on interpretation. OpenEval finds the dimerization claims (C38, C79-C84, C88, C215-C216) strongly supported by multiple biophysical methods. Peer reviewers express major concerns about physiological relevance, with Reviewer 2 stating the possibility of artifact 'has not been ruled out' and questioning the credibility of the parallel dimer if the antiparallel is dismissed as artifactual.

Disagreement on biological relevance. OpenEval supports the structural observation of two dimeric configurations (C45-C48) and finds the inference about parallel dimer physiological relevance reasonable. Peer reviewers question the biological relevance of both forms, noting it's 'probably impossible to distinguish these in the AUC experiments' and that dismissing the antiparallel dimer undermines confidence in the parallel arrangement.

Agreement on structural observations. Both evaluations support the structural characterization of the resting state conformation (C52-C56, C202, C205-C206). OpenEval notes this is an inference about physiological relevance; peer reviewers accept the structural observation and note it's consistent with the elevator mechanism, with the first structure solved without a fiducial.

Disagreement on functional significance. OpenEval supports the lipid observations (C96-C98, C103, C211, C213) with functional importance as a reasonable inference. Peer reviewers acknowledge the structural observation but emphasize that functional importance is not established without experimental validation (mutagenesis), with multiple reviewers stating this conclusion is 'not supported' without disrupting the interactions.

Partial overlap on lipid observations. OpenEval supports the fusion helix pocket lipid characterization (C105-C110, C212) with specific lipid identity as an inference. This overlaps with peer R4's concerns about lipid functional claims, though peer R4 focuses more broadly on all lipid observations while OpenEval R6 specifically addresses the fusion helix pocket.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the proteoliposome transport assay data (C121-C128). OpenEval notes appropriate controls and consistency with previous work. Peer reviewers accept the functional characterization as validating the protein preparation and supporting mechanistic interpretations without significant criticism.

Agreement on stoichiometry determination. Both evaluations support the Na+ stoichiometry findings (C131-C134). OpenEval emphasizes statistical analysis and consistency with previous work. Peer reviewers do not challenge these claims, with Reviewer 3 explicitly acknowledging the identification of Na+ binding sites.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the Na+ binding site characterization (C141-C143, C146, C149). OpenEval emphasizes high-resolution structural data and validation with CheckMyMetal. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a major strength enabling precise assignment of side chains and their orientation for mechanistic studies.

Agreement on substrate binding site. Both evaluations support the characterization of the Neu5Ac binding site (C157, C159, C160). OpenEval notes improved definition relative to previous structures. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the improved resolution allowing clearer refinement of binding sites.

Agreement on binding affinity measurement. Both evaluations support the fluorescence-detected AUC determination of SiaP-HiSiaQM affinity (C171-C173). OpenEval emphasizes good model fit and consistency with previous work. Peer Reviewer 2 highlights the development of this AUC-based approach as useful for future studies.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the cross-functionality findings (C194-C196). OpenEval notes appropriate experimental design testing cross-system compatibility. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly highlights this as 'very interesting,' revealing for the first time that TRAP membrane components can recognize multiple SBPs.

Agreement on fusion helix characterization. Both evaluations support the structural observations of the fusion helix (C66-C67, C207-C209). OpenEval emphasizes clear structural observations and topology definition. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the first structure of a fused SiaQM, highlighting structural elements that could modulate transport.

Agreement on structural rationalization of mutagenesis. Both evaluations support how the high-resolution structure reinterprets previous mutagenesis data (C113-C114, C156, C161-C164 for OpenEval; C183-C186 for peer). Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'the current structure nicely explains a lot of prior mutagenesis data.'

Agreement on integration of structural and mutagenesis data. Both evaluations support the integration of structural observations with previous mutagenesis results (C181-C186). OpenEval emphasizes consistency between structure and mutagenesis strengthening both lines of evidence. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the structure explaining prior functional data.

Related to mutagenesis rationalization. OpenEval R16 addresses specific residues (C188-C191) combining mutagenesis with structural observations. This is part of the broader pattern acknowledged by peer reviewers that the structure explains prior mutagenesis data on H. influenzae TRAP.

OpenEval identifies uncertainty in the mechanistic explanation for activity differences between HiSiaQM and PpSiaQM (C135-C140), noting the ecological explanation is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims about comparative activity and temperature adaptation.

OpenEval supports the control experiment showing dimerization specificity (C91-C92). No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this control, though peer concerns about dimerization artifacts (R2) relate to the broader context of these claims.

Partial overlap on concentration-dependent behavior. OpenEval R19 supports the SEC observations of concentration-dependent elution (C40-C43) as characteristic of self-association. Peer R2 addresses the broader dimerization claims with skepticism about physiological relevance, which contextualizes these initial observations.

OpenEval supports the HiSiaP characterization and computational modeling of the complex (C177-C180), noting experimental validation is needed. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these modeling claims, though peer R9 discusses the binding affinity measurement.

OpenEval supports the sequence conservation analysis (C152-C154, C182, C190) as providing evolutionary context. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses the conservation analysis, though this underlies interpretations discussed in other peer results.

OpenEval expresses uncertainty about lipid binding site conservation claims (C111, C118), noting experimental confirmation is needed. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses the conservation of lipid binding sites, though peer R4 addresses lipid functional claims more broadly.

Related to mechanistic model. OpenEval R23 supports the integrative conclusion about the elevator mechanism (C39) as consistent with the data. Peer R12 notes the structures are consistent with the elevator mechanism, providing implicit support for this mechanistic framework.

Agreement on speculative nature. OpenEval identifies uncertainty about functional roles of structural features (C116-C117, C120, C210, C214, C222), noting these are hypotheses requiring experimental testing. Peer R4 similarly emphasizes that functional importance claims are not supported without experimental validation.

OpenEval identifies uncertainty in the kinetic interpretation of the measured KD (C227-C234), noting this represents thoughtful speculation rather than established results. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these kinetic interpretations of the binding affinity.

Related to antiparallel dimer interpretation. OpenEval R26 expresses uncertainty about the antiparallel dimer explanation (C223-C225), noting it's plausible but speculative. Peer R3 more strongly dismisses the antiparallel dimer as 'clearly not biologically relevant' and questions whether it undermines confidence in the parallel arrangement.

OpenEval identifies uncertainty about therapeutic applications (C241-C242) as representing future directions rather than current results. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these speculative application claims.
